meta.title: Cuesetter – turn run sheets into grandMA3 cue lists
meta.description: Upload a run sheet as PDF, Word or Excel and get a macro that builds a named cue list on your grandMA3 console. Runs in your browser – your files never leave your computer.
meta.appDescription: Convert a run sheet (PDF, Word or Excel) to a grandMA3 macro: check columns, review cues, download and import on the console.

nav.theme: Switch between light and dark mode

home.title: From run sheet to cue list in a minute
home.lead: Upload the run sheet you got from production – PDF, Word or Excel. Get one empty, named cue per item, in the right order, ready to import on the console.
home.privacy: Runs in your browser. Your run sheet never leaves your computer.
home.disclaimer: Not affiliated with MA Lighting. grandMA3 is a trademark of MA Lighting Technology GmbH.

upload.title: Upload the run sheet
upload.text: Drop the PDF, Word or Excel file from production, or paste the text. Columns like #, Start and Title are found automatically.

review.title: Check the cues
review.text: One row per cue, in the right order. Edit names, split a set list into sub-cues and fix anything that was read wrong.

console.title: Import on the console
console.text: Download a macro, import it on grandMA3 and run it once. Your sequence is built with named, empty cues.

home.ctaSub: Free to try. No account needed.

demo.caption: Your run sheet in, a named cue list out. Columns you don’t need are left behind.

formats.title: Reads the run sheet as it arrives
formats.text: PDF, Word or Excel, straight from production. No reformatting, no copying into a template.

private.title: Your files never leave your computer
private.text: Everything is read in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, so you can use it with confidential shows.

tested.title: Tested on grandMA3 onPC 2.5.1
tested.text: The macro is verified on the console software. We say which versions are tested, and nothing more.

industry.title: Built in the industry, for operators
industry.text: Made by people who work on shows, and tested on real run sheets.

story: Cuesetter started backstage. A friend of ours runs lights on grandMA3, and before every show the same thing happened: the run sheet arrived as a PDF, often late, and every item had to be typed into the console by hand while the lighting waited.
We work in the industry too, just not behind the desk. So we built the tool we wished our friend had, and tested it on real run sheets.
home.storySign: Built in the industry, for operators.
home.tagline: Run sheet in. Cue list out.
home.finalLead: Try it with your next run sheet, or with our sample.

upload.title: Upload a run sheet
upload.lead: PDF, Word (.docx) or Excel (.xlsx). Everything is read in your browser.
upload.dropHint: Drop a PDF, Word or Excel file here
upload.trySample: Try with a sample run sheet
upload.pasteLead: Useful for scanned PDFs, or a list from an email or a spreadsheet.
upload.noTextLayer: No text found in this PDF. It is probably scanned (an image). Copy the text manually and paste it below.
upload.noRows: No items found. Check the columns, or paste the text instead.
upload.linesMode: No column headers found, so items were read line by line. Check the result carefully.
upload.sampleError: Couldn’t load the sample run sheet. Check your connection and try again.
upload.tooLarge: The file is larger than {max} MB. Is it really a run sheet?
upload.tooLong: The text is too long ({count} of max {max} characters).
upload.oldFormat: This is an old Word or Excel file (.doc or .xls). Open it and save it as .docx or .xlsx, or export it as PDF, then try again.
upload.unsupported: This file type can’t be read. Use a PDF, Word (.docx) or Excel (.xlsx) file, or paste the text below.
upload.noTable: Found no table with run sheet items in the file. Check that it holds the plan, or paste the text below.
upload.unreadable: Couldn’t open the file. It may be damaged or password protected. Save a new copy, or paste the text below.

columns.title: Check the columns
columns.lead: These are the columns we found. Pick which ones hold the number, time and title. The rest are ignored.
columns.confirmReset: Changing the columns replaces the edits you made in the cue list. Continue?

review.lead: {cues, plural, one {# cue} other {# cues}} from {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}. Check names and numbers before you download.
review.name: Name
review.splitHint: Turn each note line into a sub-cue
review.numberingFellBack: The # column can’t be used as cue numbers (missing, invalid or not increasing), so cues are numbered 1, 2, 3 …
review.truncatedSummary: {count, plural, one {# name} other {# names}} will be shortened to {max} characters on the console.
review.emptyLead: Add a cue by hand, or start over with another run sheet.
review.numbersFilled: {count, plural, one {# cue had} other {# cues had}} no # in the run sheet and got a number between its neighbours (for example 28.5). The rest keep their #.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Sensible defaults are already set, so you can go straight on.
settings.sequenceHelp: If the sequence already exists, the console asks to merge or overwrite.
settings.sequenceInvalid: Use a whole number from 1 to 99999.
settings.noteText: Rest of the title (set list, details)
settings.clearFirstHelp: Recommended. Makes sure the cues are stored empty.
settings.sequenceNameEmpty: Without a name the macro is called “Run sheet”.

export.title: Ready to export
export.lead: Sequence {sequence} · {cues, plural, one {# cue} other {# cues}} · {version}
export.verified: Tested on grandMA3 onPC 2.5.1.0. Other versions are not tested yet – try it in onPC before using it on a show.
export.how1: Unzip to the root of a USB stick (the grandMA3 folder goes at the top).
export.how2: Insert the stick in the console.
export.how3: Open {menu}, choose Macros and the USB stick as source.
export.how4: Import “{file}” into a free slot in the Macros pool.
export.how5: Run the macro once. It builds sequence {sequence}.
export.cmdLead: If the import fails, paste this straight into the command line.
export.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy automatically. Select the text and copy it by hand.
export.downloadError: Couldn’t create the file. Try again.

errors.notFoundLead: The link may be old or mistyped.
errors.errorLead: The page hit an unexpected error. Your files never left your computer.
